title: Introduction to the Motoko Language
section: 38. Build Your First Defi (Decentralised Finance) DApp - DBANK
summary: Creates the DBANK project with the dfx SDK, then builds a first Motoko actor from scratch: a mutable balance variable, reassignment with :=, an immutable let constant, importing the Debug module, and printing values with debug_show. Ends with a small challenge to print the constant.

concepts.heading: Creating the project
points: Work from the folder set up earlier for IC projects (cd into it), then run `dfx new dbank`. The SDK scaffolds the whole project; it takes roughly 2-5 minutes depending on the machine.
Open the new folder in the code editor. Notable items: README, a git repo, node_modules/config files (ignore these), and src, where all code goes.
The backend file is a main.mo (Motoko) with starter code. Delete the contents so everything is written from scratch.
(Extra) The reference repo was generated with a newer dfx template, so the backend folder is src/DBANK_backend/main.mo and a frontend canister sits beside it; dfx.json lists both canisters.

concepts.heading: The actor (canister) skeleton
points: In Motoko, the unit that becomes a canister is an `actor`. Write the actor keyword, a name (here DBank), and a block in braces. That alone defines a canister.
Inside the actor most ordinary programming ideas apply, and every statement ends with a semicolon.
(Extra) The reference code writes `persistent actor DBank { ... }`; newer Motoko versions use the persistent keyword so state survives upgrades by default.

concepts.heading: Variables, naming and reassignment
points: `var currentValue = 300;` declares a mutable variable holding the bank balance, starting at 300.

Naming convention from the Motoko style guide: lowerCamelCase for variables, constants and anything dynamic; UpperCamelCase for actors, modules and types. The guide also recommends two-space indentation. These are style conventions and don't change how the code runs.
Reassignment uses `:=`, not `=`. `currentValue := 100;` replaces the stored value, so after that line the variable holds 100. A single `=` is only for the initial declaration.

concepts.heading: Debugging output with Debug.print
points: The Debug module lives in the Motoko base library. Import with `import Debug "mo:base/Debug";` where `mo:` marks a Motoko package, `base` is the base library, then the module name.
`Debug.print("Hello")` writes text to the terminal that runs the local replica, similar to console.log.
print only accepts Text. Passing the number variable gives a type mismatch error because currentValue is a Nat (natural number: whole, non-negative).
Wrap non-text values in `debug_show(...)` to convert them to text for printing: `Debug.print(debug_show(currentValue))`. Large numbers print with underscore thousands separators.

concepts.heading: Running it locally
points: Terminal 1: `dfx start` launches the local Internet Computer simulation (served on localhost, port 8000 in the lecture) and must stay running.
Terminal 2, inside the project folder: `dfx deploy` creates and installs the canister. Prints from the actor appear in terminal 1 at deploy time.
Edit, save, run `dfx deploy` again to see updated output.

concepts.heading: let for constants
points: `let id = 3244896453846;` declares an immutable binding, like const in JavaScript. Use it for data that must never change.
Trying `id := ...` fails at compile time because it is immutable.

task.name: Print the constant id
task.starting_point: The actor from this lesson with currentValue, the let id constant and a Debug.print("Hello") line, deployed locally.
task.goal: Make the id constant show up in the terminal output.
steps: Pause and make sure the lesson code is written locally.
Call Debug.print with debug_show(id) as the argument (plain id would be a type error).
Save and run dfx deploy in the second terminal; check the first terminal for the number.
task.expected_result: The terminal prints the large id number with underscore separators.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 38 - Build Your First Defi (Decentralised Finance) DApp - DBANK/38.02 Introduction to the Motoko Language/DBANK/src/DBANK_backend/main.mo

pitfalls: Passing a Nat directly to Debug.print causes a type mismatch; use debug_show.
Trying to reassign a let constant.
Running dfx deploy in the same terminal as dfx start (stops the replica); use a second terminal.
Forgetting the semicolon at the end of statements.
